issues.title: eval --json: scalar and object results have inconsistent type in output.result

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
browser4-cli eval --json "document.title" → output.result = "Interactive Single Page" (plain string).
browser4-cli eval --json "({x:1})" → output.result = "{\"x\":1}" (JSON-encoded string requiring JSON.parse).

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: output.result should have a consistent type regardless of the JavaScript expression return type. Either always the raw value, or always a JSON-encoded string. A consumer should not need to introspect the result to decide whether to JSON.parse() it.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: For scalar expressions (strings, numbers, booleans, null), output.result is the raw value. For object/array expressions, output.result is a JSON-encoded string. This requires type-dependent parsing logic: check if result starts with '{' or '[', then JSON.parse; otherwise use directly.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The serialization path appears to JSON-stringify objects (as documented: 'Objects and arrays are serialized as JSON') before storing them in output.result, but scalars are stored directly. The --json flag wraps the overall output in a JSON envelope but doesn't normalize the result field type.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Always store the result as a JSON-encoded string in output.result (strings get quoted, numbers stay as numbers in JSON, objects get stringified). Consumers then always JSON.parse(output.result).
- Or, alternatively, always store the raw parsed value — but this may not be possible with JSON envelope constraints.
- Document the expected parse strategy clearly in --help output.

issues.title: page-info command is minimal — no element counts or metadata beyond title/URL

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: browser4-cli page-info

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: page-info should provide useful at-a-glance page metadata: title, URL, link count, image count, form count, maybe script count or page size.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Only shows Title and URL. A user wanting link count must fall back to eval: browser4-cli eval "document.querySelectorAll('a').length".

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: page-info only extracts the page title and URL from the browser. It doesn't query the DOM for element counts. Adding DOM queries for common element types would make the command much more useful for first-time exploration.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add link count (document.links.length), image count (document.images.length), and form count (document.forms.length) to page-info output.
- Consider adding a --verbose flag for richer metadata (script count, stylesheet count, DOM node count, page size estimate).

issues.title: No built-in command to count page elements (links, images, forms)

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Try to get the number of links on a page without using eval.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A discoverable command or flag for quick page statistics: link count, image count, form count, heading count.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The user must discover and construct eval expressions: document.querySelectorAll('a').length, document.images.length, document.forms.length. No built-in command or shortcut exists.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Page statistics are only available via JavaScript eval. A wrapper command or page-info enhancement could expose these common queries without requiring JavaScript knowledge.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Extend page-info with a --stats flag that returns link/image/form/script/heading counts.
- Add a 'stats' subcommand that returns these counts as structured JSON.
- Consider adding it as an alias or shortcut so users don't need to write JavaScript for basic page analysis.

issues.title: Footgun suggestion text contains syntactically incorrect fix

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: browser4-cli eval "element.textContent" --ref e5

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The suggestion should propose a correct fix: "element => element.textContent"

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The tip reads: "Did you mean: eval \"element => element.element.textContent\" --ref …?" — the expression "element.element.textContent" is nonsensical (element.element would be undefined).

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The suggestion generator appears to prepend "element => element." to the original expression, but the original is already "element.textContent", producing "element => element.element.textContent". The generator should detect and strip the leading "element." before prepending the arrow function wrapper.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Detect when the user's expression starts with "element." and generate "element => element.textContent" instead of "element => element.element.textContent".
- Or simply always suggest the fixed form explicitly without string concatenation: "Use: eval \"element => element.textContent\" --ref e5"

issues.title: Session reuse from prior test runs may confuse first-time users

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run goto after a previous session was left open: browser4-cli goto "http://localhost:18080/generated/interactive-1.html"

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Either a clean session or a clear indication that a prior session is being reused, with guidance on how to start fresh.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Output shows "Using existing session DEFAULT (current page: http://localhost:18080/generated/form-filling.html)" — a first-time user might not understand why a session already exists or whether this is normal.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The session persists between CLI invocations by design. The message informs about reuse but doesn't explain what it means or how to start clean.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add a brief one-line explanation: "Sessions persist between commands. Use 'close' to end the session or 'goto' to navigate elsewhere."
- Consider a --fresh flag on goto to force a new session.
- Show the session reuse message only when the previous page differs from the target URL.

issues.title: snapshot -i includes non-interactive elements misleading users about what 'interactive' means

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: browser4-cli snapshot -i --stdout

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Based on the flag name "-i" (interactive), a user expects to see ONLY truly interactive elements: buttons, links, inputs, selects, textareas.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Output also includes headings (h1, h2), paragraphs, LabelText elements, and generic containers with ARIA roles. These are not interactive — they can't be clicked, filled, or selected. The flag actually strips 'generic <div>, <span>, and other non-interactive containers' as documented, but the flag name '-i'/'--interactive' implies more aggressive filtering.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The flag name '--interactive' is misleading. The implementation filters based on AX role heuristics (stripping generic containers) rather than interactivity. The documentation does clarify this, but the flag name creates a wrong expectation.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Rename the flag to better match its behavior, e.g. --no-containers or --essential, or clarify with a longer name like --interactive-plus-labels.
- Or add a stricter mode that truly shows only clickable/fillable elements.
- At minimum, add a brief note in the --help text: "Note: -i does not strip headings, paragraphs, or labels — use snapshot grep to filter further."

issues.title: eval --file behavior with multi-statement scripts is undocumented

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Write a file with multiple statements ending in an expression (e.g. 'const x = 1; x'), then run: browser4-cli eval --file script.js

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Documentation should clearly state whether multi-statement scripts are supported and how the return value is determined (last expression? explicit return?).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: It works — the last expression's value is returned. But this behavior is not documented. The examples only show single expressions. Users might assume only single expressions work.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The --help text only shows single-expression examples. The Runtime.evaluate call likely evaluates the entire script and returns the completion value, but this is an implementation detail users shouldn't need to guess.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add a note to --help: 'Multi-statement scripts are supported; the value of the last expression is returned.'
- Add an example: browser4-cli eval --file script.js where script.js contains multiple statements.
- Clarify that console.log() output is not captured — only the return value.
